text:
dashsplat

dashsplat rebuilds the world around a car as an orbitable 3D scene from the six dashcam cameras of a Tesla: it
calibrates the cameras from the footage, fits Gaussian splats and a 1 cm road texture to the photographs, tracks the
other vehicles, and redraws the view from behind the car with a one-step image model. It was built in one day and
one night by a team of AI coding agents directed by Ryan Vogel, from one drive of his own Model 3 (HW4), and it is
slow, rough and tuned to that one car.

 

 The test drive at 112 s in the web viewer, with the generated chase view. The same moment drawn from the splats
alone: 112-splat.jpg. The on-screen HUD imitates Tesla's display; see
docs/NAMING.md. 

This is an independent hobby project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Tesla, Inc. The footage
it was built from is the author's own, recorded by his own car.

 Status

Work in progress, one day old. It has run on exactly one recording: a 6-minute, 3.3 km drive at dawn under
overcast sky (361.44 s, of which 249.53 s moving). Every number below comes from a report in this repository,
linked beside it. Those reports were written as the work happened, so they use the working name "Reality Splat",
refer to the author's machines ("the Studio" is his Mac Studio with an M5 Ultra, "basebook" his working Mac), and some
link to large videos and private folders ( out/ , scratch/ ) that are not included. TIMELINE.md
lists every commit of the original history.

 What it does

 Stage What it does Result on the test drive 
 --- --- --- 
 Ingest (pipeline/ingest) Decodes all six cameras and reads the telemetry Tesla embeds in every frame (speed, heading, GPS, steering, pedals, blinkers, driver-assist state); dead-reckons a trajectory The dead-reckoned track ends 7.5 m from GPS after 3.3 km. The telemetry has no height, pitch or roll (PLAN.md) 
 Calibration (pipeline/calib) Solves each lens, its position on the car, clock offset and rolling shutter from the footage itself, with no factory data Inlier reprojection error 0.81 to 0.97 px per lens; a held-out scale check came out 2.14 % off the telemetry, missing the 1 % goal (report) 
 Poses (pipeline/poses) A 6-degree-of-freedom trajectory for the whole drive from telemetry plus images All 12,927 front-camera timestamps; whole-drive reprojection error 1.5 to 1.8 px. Points seen far ahead land tens of pixels off when the car arrives (report) 
 Road (pipeline/road) Road-relative attitude and a bird's-eye mosaic, the base of the ground layer 0 of 41 measured cells met their centimetre targets; final offline medians 9 to 14 cm (report) 
 Depth and masks (pipeline/depth, pipeline/masks) Metric depth from pose-conditioned models (Depth Anything 3, MapAnything) and sky, road and vehicle masks (Mask2Former) Front camera: scale within 4 to 5 %, temporal error 1.8 % over 1 m of travel. Every monocular "metric" model tried was off by 15 to 70 % (report) 
 Ground atlas (pipeline/groundtex) The road as a photographic texture on a height mesh, one photograph per texel, every texel labelled observed or predicted Road at 1 to 2 cm per texel, verges at 4 cm out to 40 m; 53.1 % of the ground within 40 m is predicted, not photographed (report) 
 Splat scenes (pipeline/livemap, pipeline/stitch) Trees, poles and buildings as Gaussian splats, fitted to the photographs and to "teacher" views re-projected from them Published, "not ready for a side-by-side with Tesla's screen": crowns smear, traffic lights hang without arms, two named office buildings do not read as buildings. 4.08 million object splats in 85 to 140 s (report) 
 Movers (pipeline/movers) Each tracked vehicle as a rigid splat model moving along a smoothed track; the viewer draws clean stand-in models by default 23 moving episodes and nine fixed models in the published scene; a bus passing behind trees is not readable (report) 
 Generated chase view (pipeline/genfill) Renders the chase camera, then NVIDIA's Difix-ref redraws each frame from the render plus the nearest real photograph in one diffusion step; observed road paint is put back exactly and every pixel is labelled 3,183 frames over 93 to 140, 190 to 215 and 296 to 330 s. Flicker below the real camera's; sky invented in about a quarter of each frame; signs come out as garbled text (report, sections 11 to 13) 
 Viewer (viewer) three.js and Spark in the browser: streams tiles, plays the drive back, Live, Stitched, Memory and Generative modes 60 fps at 3200x2000 in Chrome on an Apple M5 Max (viewer/README.md) 
 One command (pipeline/run) Raw clips to a published scene, resumable, every stage checked Preview tier for the whole drive, no manual step; full tier on a 30 s window and part of the whole drive 
 NVIDIA port (pipeline/cuda) The same command on Linux with CUDA, replacing the two Apple-only stages Ran end to end on one rented L40S; not at parity with the Mac result (below) 

 

 A lane line in the first ground splats, in the ground atlas, and in one front-camera photograph
(pipeline/groundtex/REPORT.md). 

Things that did not work are kept with their reports: showing re-projected photographs directly fails when depth is
wrong (pipeline/ibr/REPORT.md; it became the teacher for the splats instead), a driving
video model (StreetNVS) moves the lane paint, with 9 of 73 checks within 3 px
(pipeline/genvideo/REPORT.md), and a sky map from the six cameras is 78 % invented
because no camera looks up (pipeline/envmap/report/REPORT.md).

 How long it takes

Stage time per minute of moving footage, from pipeline/run/README.md (Mac Studio, M5
Ultra) and pipeline/cuda/README.md (one NVIDIA L40S at $1.11 an hour with 13.6 CPU cores):

 Tier M5 Ultra L40S 
 --- ---: ---: 
 Preview: ground splats, road atlas, automatic vehicle tracks 13.6 min (whole drive) 32.9 min, $0.61 
 Full geometry: production depth and masks, vehicle removal, teacher views, splat fit 51.9 min (first windows of the whole drive) 82.9 min, $1.54
